123	          "verbatim": "/// Re-encrypt a file's `FileMetadata` IPNS record from `source_folder_key` to\n/// `dest_folder_key` after a cross-folder move (fire-and-forget).\n///\n/// A file's `FileMetadata` is sealed with its PARENT folder's AES key. The rename\n/// handlers only republish the old/new *folder* metadata; the per-file record\n/// stays sealed under the source key. Without this, any fresh resolve under the\n/// destination folder's key — a remount, another device, or the web client —\n/// fails with a decryption error. This resolves the current record under the\n/// source key and republishes the SAME metadata sealed under the destination key\n/// (no version bump). Mirrors the SDK `moveItem` re-encrypt step.\n#[cfg(any(feature = \"fuse\", feature = \"winfsp\"))]\n#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]\npub fn spawn_file_meta_reencrypt(\n    api: Arc<ApiClient>,\n    rt: tokio::runtime::Handle,\n    file_meta_ipns_name: String,\n    file_ipns_private_key: Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>,\n    source_folder_key: Vec<u8>,\n    dest_folder_key: Vec<u8>,\n    coordinator: Arc<PublishCoordinator>,\n    tee_public_key: Option<Vec<u8>>,\n    tee_key_epoch: Option<u32>,\n) {\n    // Distinct folders always carry distinct keys; this guard is purely defensive\n    // and skips a needless resolve+publish (and sequence bump) if they ever match.\n    if source_folder_key == dest_folder_key {\n        return;\n    }\n    std::thread::spawn(move || {\n        let result = rt.block_on(async {\n            let source_key_arr: [u8; 32] = source_folder_key\n                .as_slice()\n                .try_into()\n                .map_err(|_| \"Invalid source folder key length\".to_string())?;\n\n            // Serialize against concurrent publishes to the same file IPNS record.\n            let lock = coordinator.get_lock(&file_meta_ipns_name);\n            let _guard = lock.lock().await;\n\n            // Resolve the CURRENT FileMetadata under the SOURCE folder key.\n            let resp = cipherbox_api_client::ipns::resolve_ipns(&api, &file_meta_ipns_name)\n                .await\n                .map_err(|e| format!(\"resolve file IPNS: {}\", e))?;\n            let enc_bytes = cipherbox_api_client::ipfs::fetch_content(&api, &resp.cid)\n                .await\n                .map_err(|e| format!(\"fetch file metadata: {}\", e))?;\n            let file_meta =\n                cipherbox_core::decrypt_file_metadata_from_ipfs_public(&enc_bytes, &source_key_arr)\n                    .map_err(|e| format!(\"decrypt file metadata under source key: {}\", e))?;\n\n            // Republish the SAME metadata sealed under the DESTINATION key. The\n            // record already exists, so this is an update (seq + 1), no TEE enroll.\n            publish_file_metadata(\n                &api,\n                &file_meta,\n                &dest_folder_key,\n                &file_ipns_private_key,\n                &file_meta_ipns_name,\n                coordinator.as_ref(),\n                tee_public_key.as_deref(),\n                tee_key_epoch,\n                false,\n            )\n            .await\n            .map_err(|e| format!(\"re-publish file metadata under dest key: {}\", e))?;\n\n            log::info!(\n                \"Re-encrypted file metadata for {} after cross-folder move\",\n                file_meta_ipns_name\n            );\n            Ok::<(), String>(())\n        });\n        if let Err(e) = result {\n            log::error!(\"File metadata re-encrypt on move failed: {}\", e);\n        }\n    });\n}"

1	/**
2	 * TDD test: moveItem must re-encrypt FileMetadata with the destination folder key.
3	 *
4	 * Root cause: FileMetadata is AES-256-GCM encrypted with the parent folder's key
5	 * at upload time. When a file is moved to a folder with a different key, the
6	 * FileMetadata IPNS record must be re-published encrypted with the destination
7	 * folder key — otherwise all decrypt operations (download, preview, edit) fail
8	 * with "Decryption failed" because they supply the destination folder key.
9	 *
10	 * This test is RED before the fix (moveItem does not call resolveFileMetadata /
11	 * updateFileMetadata) and GREEN after (moveItem re-encrypts on move).
12	 */

324	/**
325	 * Restore an item from the recycle bin back to a folder.
326	 *
327	 * Removes the entry from bin metadata, adds the preserved FolderChild
328	 * back to the target folder's children, and publishes both.
329	 */
330	export async function restoreFromBin(params: {
331	  entryId: string;
332	  targetFolderIpnsName: string;
333	  folderTree: FolderTree;
334	  binState: BinState;
335	  binCtx: BinOperationContext;
336	}): Promise<{ restoredItem: FolderChild; updatedBinState: BinState }> {
337	  // 1. Find the bin entry
338	  const entry = params.binState.entries.find((e) => e.id === params.entryId);
339	  if (!entry) throw new Error('Bin entry not found');
340	
341	  // 2. Get the FolderChild to restore
342	  let child: FolderChild;
343	  if (entry.itemType === 'file' && entry.filePointer) {
344	    child = { ...entry.filePointer, modifiedAt: Date.now() };
345	  } else if (entry.itemType === 'folder' && entry.folderEntry) {
346	    child = { ...entry.folderEntry, modifiedAt: Date.now() };
347	  } else {
348	    throw new Error('Bin entry has no stored item reference');
349	  }
350	
351	  // 3. Add child back to target folder
352	  const targetFolder = params.folderTree.get(params.targetFolderIpnsName);
353	  if (!targetFolder) throw new Error('Target folder not loaded');
354	
355	  // Handle name collisions
356	  const existingNames = new Set(targetFolder.children.map((c) => c.name));
357	  if (existingNames.has(child.name)) {
358	    let newName = `${child.name} (restored)`;
359	    let counter = 2;
360	    while (existingNames.has(newName)) {
361	      newName = `${child.name} (restored ${counter})`;
362	      counter++;
363	    }
364	    child = { ...child, name: newName };
365	  }
366	
367	  // 3b. Re-encrypt the file's FileMetadata IPNS record for the destination folder
368	  // when restoring to a DIFFERENT folder than the original parent. The record is
369	  // AES-256-GCM encrypted with the folderKey of wherever the file lived when
370	  // deleted (entry.originalParentIpnsName); addToBin stores the FilePointer
371	  // verbatim and never re-encrypts. Restoring to a folder with a different
372	  // folderKey without re-encrypting would make the file undecryptable
373	  // (CryptoError: Decryption failed) — the same class of bug as moveItem. When
374	  // restoring in place (target === original parent, the default UI flow) the key
375	  // is unchanged, so this is a no-op and we skip it. Run this BEFORE the folder
376	  // publish so a failure aborts the restore with no partial state.
377	  if (
378	    entry.itemType === 'file' &&
379	    entry.filePointer &&
380	    params.targetFolderIpnsName !== entry.originalParentIpnsName
381	  ) {
382	    // Unwrapped key material is cleared in `finally`. Only the freshly
383	    // unwrapped source key is zeroed — never the shared folderTree key from the
384	    // legacy fallback, which the tree still owns.
385	    let unwrappedSourceFolderKey: Uint8Array | undefined;
386	    let fileIpnsPrivateKey: Uint8Array | undefined;
387	    try {
388	      // Source key = the folderKey the FileMetadata is currently encrypted under.
389	      // Prefer the key captured on the entry at delete time (works even if the
390	      // original parent no longer exists); fall back to the live folder tree for
391	      // legacy entries created before originalFolderKeyEncrypted was captured.
392	      let sourceFolderKey: Uint8Array;
393	      if (entry.originalFolderKeyEncrypted) {
394	        unwrappedSourceFolderKey = await unwrapKey(
395	          hexToBytes(entry.originalFolderKeyEncrypted),
396	          params.binCtx.userPrivateKey
397	        );
398	        sourceFolderKey = unwrappedSourceFolderKey;
399	      } else {
400	        const sourceFolder = params.folderTree.get(entry.originalParentIpnsName);
401	        if (!sourceFolder) {
402	          throw new Error(
403	            'Original parent folder must be loaded to restore a legacy file to a different folder'
404	          );
405	        }
406	        sourceFolderKey = sourceFolder.folderKey;
407	      }
408	      if (!entry.filePointer.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted) {
409	        throw new Error('Cannot re-encrypt file metadata on restore: missing file IPNS key');
410	      }
411	      fileIpnsPrivateKey = await unwrapKey(
412	        hexToBytes(entry.filePointer.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted),
413	        params.binCtx.userPrivateKey
414	      );
415	      const { metadata: currentMetadata } = await sdkCore.resolveFileMetadata(
416	        entry.filePointer.fileMetaIpnsName,
417	        sourceFolderKey,
418	        params.binCtx.ctx
419	      );
420	      await sdkCore.updateFileMetadata({
421	        fileIpnsPrivateKey,
422	        fileMetaIpnsName: entry.filePointer.fileMetaIpnsName,
423	        folderKey: targetFolder.folderKey,
424	        currentMetadata,
425	        updates: {},
426	        createVersion: false,
427	        ctx: params.binCtx.ctx,
428	      });
429	    } finally {
430	      if (unwrappedSourceFolderKey) clearBytes(unwrappedSourceFolderKey);
431	      if (fileIpnsPrivateKey) clearBytes(fileIpnsPrivateKey);
432	    }
433	  }
434	
435	  const baseChildren = [...targetFolder.children];
436	  const updatedFolderChildren = [...targetFolder.children, child];
437	
438	  // 4. Publish updated folder metadata
439	  const { newSequenceNumber, publishedChildren } = await sdkCore.updateFolderMetadataAndPublish({
440	    children: updatedFolderChildren,
441	    baseChildren,
442	    folderKey: targetFolder.folderKey,
443	    ipnsPrivateKey: targetFolder.ipnsKeypair.privateKey,
444	    ipnsName: params.targetFolderIpnsName,
445	    sequenceNumber: targetFolder.sequenceNumber,
446	    ctx: params.binCtx.ctx,
447	  });
448	
449	  // 5. Update folder state — adopt merged published set (CR-01)
450	  targetFolder.children = publishedChildren;
451	  targetFolder.sequenceNumber = newSequenceNumber;
452	  targetFolder.lastLoadedAt = Date.now();
453	  params.folderTree.set(params.targetFolderIpnsName, targetFolder);
454	
455	  // 6. Remove entry from bin and publish
456	  const remainingEntries = params.binState.entries.filter((e) => e.id !== params.entryId);
457	  const newBinSeq = params.binState.sequenceNumber + 1;
458	
459	  const metadata: RecycleBinMetadata = {
460	    version: BIN_METADATA_VERSION,
461	    sequenceNumber: newBinSeq,
462	    entries: remainingEntries,
463	  };
464	
465	  await saveBinMetadata({ metadata, binCtx: params.binCtx });
466	
467	  const updatedBinState: BinState = {
468	    entries: remainingEntries,
469	    sequenceNumber: newBinSeq,
470	    ipnsName: params.binState.ipnsName,
471	  };
472	
473	  return { restoredItem: child, updatedBinState };
474	}
475

690	/// Re-encrypt a file's `FileMetadata` IPNS record from `source_folder_key` to
691	/// `dest_folder_key` after a cross-folder move (fire-and-forget).
692	///
693	/// A file's `FileMetadata` is sealed with its PARENT folder's AES key. The rename
694	/// handlers only republish the old/new *folder* metadata; the per-file record
695	/// stays sealed under the source key. Without this, any fresh resolve under the
696	/// destination folder's key — a remount, another device, or the web client —
697	/// fails with a decryption error. This resolves the current record under the
698	/// source key and republishes the SAME metadata sealed under the destination key
699	/// (no version bump). Mirrors the SDK `moveItem` re-encrypt step.
700	#[cfg(any(feature = "fuse", feature = "winfsp"))]
701	#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
702	pub fn spawn_file_meta_reencrypt(
703	    api: Arc<ApiClient>,
704	    rt: tokio::runtime::Handle,
705	    file_meta_ipns_name: String,
706	    file_ipns_private_key: Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>,
707	    source_folder_key: Vec<u8>,
708	    dest_folder_key: Vec<u8>,
709	    coordinator: Arc<PublishCoordinator>,
710	    tee_public_key: Option<Vec<u8>>,
711	    tee_key_epoch: Option<u32>,
712	) {
713	    // Distinct folders always carry distinct keys; this guard is purely defensive
714	    // and skips a needless resolve+publish (and sequence bump) if they ever match.
715	    if source_folder_key == dest_folder_key {
716	        return;
717	    }
718	    std::thread::spawn(move || {
719	        let result = rt.block_on(async {
720	            let source_key_arr: [u8; 32] = source_folder_key
721	                .as_slice()
722	                .try_into()
723	                .map_err(|_| "Invalid source folder key length".to_string())?;
724	
725	            // Serialize against concurrent publishes to the same file IPNS record.
726	            let lock = coordinator.get_lock(&file_meta_ipns_name);
727	            let _guard = lock.lock().await;
728	
729	            // Resolve the CURRENT FileMetadata under the SOURCE folder key.
730	            let resp = cipherbox_api_client::ipns::resolve_ipns(&api, &file_meta_ipns_name)
731	                .await
732	                .map_err(|e| format!("resolve file IPNS: {}", e))?;
733	            let enc_bytes = cipherbox_api_client::ipfs::fetch_content(&api, &resp.cid)
734	                .await
735	                .map_err(|e| format!("fetch file metadata: {}", e))?;
736	            let file_meta =
737	                cipherbox_core::decrypt_file_metadata_from_ipfs_public(&enc_bytes, &source_key_arr)
738	                    .map_err(|e| format!("decrypt file metadata under source key: {}", e))?;
739	
740	            // Republish the SAME metadata sealed under the DESTINATION key. The
741	            // record already exists, so this is an update (seq + 1), no TEE enroll.
742	            publish_file_metadata(
743	                &api,
744	                &file_meta,
745	                &dest_folder_key,
746	                &file_ipns_private_key,
747	                &file_meta_ipns_name,
748	                coordinator.as_ref(),
749	                tee_public_key.as_deref(),
750	                tee_key_epoch,
751	                false,
752	            )
753	            .await
754	            .map_err(|e| format!("re-publish file metadata under dest key: {}", e))?;
755	
756	            log::info!(
757	                "Re-encrypted file metadata for {} after cross-folder move",
758	                file_meta_ipns_name
759	            );
760	            Ok::<(), String>(())
761	        });
762	        if let Err(e) = result {
763	            log::error!("File metadata re-encrypt on move failed: {}", e);
764	        }
765	    });
766	}
767

{

  "content": "/**\n * @cipherbox/sdk - FileMetadata re-encryption on folder change\n *\n * A file's per-file `FileMetadata` IPNS record is AES-256-GCM sealed with its\n * PARENT folder's `folderKey`; the decrypt path uses the key of whichever folder\n * lists the pointer. Whenever a file changes parent folder — a cross-folder\n * `moveItem`, or a `restoreFromBin` to a folder other than the original parent —\n * the record must be re-sealed under the destination `folderKey`, or every later\n * decrypt under that folder fails with `CryptoError: Decryption failed`.\n *\n * Shared by `CipherBoxClient.moveItem` and `restoreFromBin` so both paths get the\n * same idempotent retry semantics.\n */\n\nimport * as sdkCore from '@cipherbox/sdk-core';\nimport type { SdkContext } from '@cipherbox/sdk-core';\nimport type { FileMetadata } from '@cipherbox/core';\n\n/**\n * True for the AES-GCM wrong-key decrypt failure (`CryptoError` with code\n * `'DECRYPTION_FAILED'`, from `@cipherbox/crypto`).\n *\n * Matches the `.code`, not the message: the message is intentionally generic to\n * avoid a padding oracle, so it is not a reliable discriminator. Duck-typed on\n * `.code` rather than `instanceof CryptoError` so the check can never throw under\n * a partial test mock of `@cipherbox/crypto`, and so a missing-record error\n * (a plain `Error` with no `.code`) correctly does NOT match.\n */\nfunction isDecryptionFailure(err: unknown): boolean {\n  return err instanceof Error && (err as { code?: unknown }).code === 'DECRYPTION_FAILED';\n}\n\n/**\n * Re-seal a file's `FileMetadata` IPNS record from `sourceFolderKey` to\n * `destFolderKey` (no version bump — re-keying is not a content change).\n *\n * Idempotent. If the record no longer decrypts under the source key, a prior\n * partial attempt may have already re-keyed it to the destination: this confirms\n * the record decrypts under the destination key and, if so, treats the\n * re-encryption as already complete (so a retry after a partial failure finishes\n * the move cleanly instead of throwing). A genuinely unreadable record — missing,\n * or undecryptable under BOTH keys — propagates the original error.\n *\n * Does NOT own `fileIpnsPrivateKey`: the caller unwraps it and clears it in a\n * `finally`. `updateFileMetadata` zeroes it on the re-key path; on the\n * already-re-keyed path it is never consumed, so the caller's `finally` is the\n * only thing that clears it.\n */\nexport async function reencryptFileMetadataForFolderChange(params: {\n  fileMetaIpnsName: string;\n  fileIpnsPrivateKey: Uint8Array;\n  sourceFolderKey: Uint8Array;\n  destFolderKey: Uint8Array;\n  ctx: SdkContext;\n}): Promise<void> {\n  let currentMetadata: FileMetadata;\n  try {\n    ({ metadata: currentMetadata } = await sdkCore.resolveFileMetadata(\n      params.fileMetaIpnsName,\n      params.sourceFolderKey,\n      params.ctx\n    ));\n  } catch (err) {\n    if (!isDecryptionFailure(err)) throw err;\n    // Source-key decrypt failed. A prior partial attempt may have already\n    // re-keyed the record to the destination — confirm by resolving under the\n    // destination key. Success ⇒ re-encryption already done (idempotent retry);\n    // failure ⇒ the record is genuinely unreadable and the original error stands.\n    try {\n      await sdkCore.resolveFileMetadata(params.fileMetaIpnsName, params.destFolderKey, params.ctx);\n    } catch {\n      throw err;\n    }\n    return;\n  }\n\n  await sdkCore.updateFileMetadata({\n    fileIpnsPrivateKey: params.fileIpnsPrivateKey,\n    fileMetaIpnsName: params.fileMetaIpnsName,\n    folderKey: params.destFolderKey,\n    currentMetadata,\n    updates: {},\n    createVersion: false,\n    ctx: params.ctx,\n  });\n}\n"
}

  "new_string": "/// Bounded retry budget for the fire-and-forget re-encrypt on cross-folder move.\n/// Mirrors the durable journal's bounded-retry-then-park bound (D-09).\n#[cfg(any(feature = \"fuse\", feature = \"winfsp\"))]\nconst REENCRYPT_MAX_ATTEMPTS: u32 = 5;\n\n/// Outcome of a single re-encrypt attempt, used to decide whether to retry.\n#[cfg(any(feature = \"fuse\", feature = \"winfsp\"))]\nenum ReencryptOutcome {\n    /// Re-keyed to the destination on this attempt.\n    Done,\n    /// A prior attempt already re-keyed the record; nothing left to do.\n    AlreadyDone,\n    /// Transient failure (resolve/fetch/publish) — worth retrying.\n    Retry(String),\n    /// Deterministic failure (undecryptable under BOTH keys) — retrying can't help.\n    Terminal(String),\n}\n\n/// Resolve a file's IPNS record and fetch its current encrypted metadata bytes.\n#[cfg(any(feature = \"fuse\", feature = \"winfsp\"))]\nasync fn resolve_and_fetch_file_meta(\n    api: &ApiClient,\n    file_meta_ipns_name: &str,\n) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {\n    let resp = cipherbox_api_client::ipns::resolve_ipns(api, file_meta_ipns_name)\n        .await\n        .map_err(|e| format!(\"resolve file IPNS: {}\", e))?;\n    let enc_bytes = cipherbox_api_client::ipfs::fetch_content(api, &resp.cid)\n        .await\n        .map_err(|e| format!(\"fetch file metadata: {}\", e))?;\n    Ok(enc_bytes)\n}\n\n/// Re-encrypt a file's `FileMetadata` IPNS record from `source_folder_key` to\n/// `dest_folder_key` after a cross-folder move (fire-and-forget)."
}

  "content": "---\ncreated: 2026-06-17T00:00:00.000Z\ncompleted: 2026-06-18T00:00:00.000Z\ntitle: Make move/restore file-metadata re-encryption recoverable across partial failures\narea: reliability\nseverity: medium\nsource: CodeRabbit CLI review of PR fix/decrypt-fail-after-move (#507)\nfiles:\n  - packages/sdk/src/reencrypt.ts\n  - packages/sdk/src/client.ts\n  - packages/sdk/src/bin/index.ts\n  - crates/fuse/src/lib.rs\n---\n\n## Problem\n\nMoving (or restoring to a different folder) a file re-encrypts its `FileMetadata`\nIPNS record from the source folderKey to the destination folderKey. This spans\n**two independent IPNS records** — the per-file `FileMetadata` record and the\nfolder metadata holding the `FilePointer` — which cannot be published atomically.\nA partial failure could strand the record (re-keyed to dest while no folder lists\nit under that key) or throw on a clean retry.\n\n## Resolution (PR #507)\n\nAll three \"when implementing\" steps below are done, plus tests.\n\n1. **Idempotent re-key helper** — extracted\n   `reencryptFileMetadataForFolderChange` (`packages/sdk/src/reencrypt.ts`), shared\n   by `moveItem` and `restoreFromBin`. If the source-key resolve throws a decrypt\n   failure (`err.code === 'DECRYPTION_FAILED'`), it confirms the record under the\n   **destination** key: success ⇒ a prior partial attempt already re-keyed it, so\n   treat the re-encryption as complete (skip the republish); failure under BOTH\n   keys ⇒ rethrow the original error. A non-decrypt error (e.g. record missing)\n   propagates without a fallback. This makes a re-run after a partial failure\n   complete instead of throwing.\n2. **`restoreFromBin` reorder** — was re-key-before-publish. Now: validate the\n   re-key preconditions up front (so a guaranteed failure aborts cleanly with no\n   broken listing), publish the target folder (add-before-remove), then re-key\n   (step 5b), then remove the bin entry. Mirrors `moveItem` (publish dest → re-key\n   → publish source): at every intermediate failure the file stays readable from\n   somewhere that lists it under the matching key — the bin (source key) before\n   the re-key, the target (target key) after — never readable from neither.\n3. **Desktop bounded retry** — `spawn_file_meta_reencrypt`\n   (`crates/fuse/src/lib.rs`) was single-attempt fire-and-forget. Now a bounded\n   in-memory retry (`REENCRYPT_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5`, exponential backoff + jitter),\n   acquiring the coordinator lock per attempt (released across the backoff sleep).\n   Transient resolve/fetch/publish errors retry; a record undecryptable under the\n   source key is checked against the **dest** key (idempotent — already re-keyed),\n   else treated as terminal and not retried. The adversarial review confirmed a **real major defect** (both reviewers, high confidence) — and it's exactly the residual I'd underestimated: my `restoreFromBin` reorder introduced a *duplicate-listing on retry*. Since step 4 publishes the target before the new step-5b re-key window, a 5b/step-6 failure leaves the entry in the bin; the retry re-adds the same child (same id, renamed) and the no-conflict publish path doesn't dedup by id → two entries for one file. `moveItem` avoids this; restore didn't. Good catch — I need to fix it before committing.

The robust fix (covers both same-session and fresh-session retries) is to make the add **idempotent by child id**. Let me read the current region precisely:

  "new_string": "  // A retry of a partially-applied restore (the bin entry survives a step-5b /\n  // step-6 failure) can find this child already listed in the target from the prior\n  // attempt's publish. Drop any prior copy by id so the restore is idempotent —\n  // re-running REPLACES rather than duplicates the listing — and exclude it from the\n  // name-collision check so the file isn't spuriously renamed against itself. The\n  // no-conflict publish path doesn't dedup by id (only the 409 merge does), so a\n  // same-id duplicate appended here would otherwise persist.\n  const targetChildrenSansChild = targetFolder.children.filter((c) => c.id !== child.id);\n\n  // Handle name collisions (against other entries only)\n  const existingNames = new Set(targetChildrenSansChild.map((c) => c.name));\n  if (existingNames.has(child.name)) {\n    let newName = `${child.name} (restored)`;\n    let counter = 2;\n    while (existingNames.has(newName)) {\n      newName = `${child.name} (restored ${counter})`;\n      counter++;\n    }\n    child = { ...child, name: newName };\n  }"
}

Verification complete. The review surfaced exactly one real defect (two reviewers, same root cause), plus it **refuted** the analogous moveItem concern (finding #3, `isReal: false` — moveItem commits dest state after the re-key, so a retry reconciles via the CAS merge). Both confirmed findings are fixed; the Rust retry and crash-safety invariant passed.

## Done — todo fully applied to PR #507 (`f6c720f48`, pushed)

**The three todo steps + the review fix:**

1. **Idempotent re-key helper** — new `packages/sdk/src/reencrypt.ts` (`reencryptFileMetadataForFolderChange`), shared by `moveItem` and `restoreFromBin`. If the source-key resolve fails to decrypt, it confirms the record under the destination key and treats the re-key as already done → a retry after a partial failure completes instead of throwing. Non-decrypt errors (missing record) propagate without a fallback.
2. **`restoreFromBin` reorder** — publish target → re-key (step 5b) → remove from bin, mirroring `moveItem`; preconditions validated up front so a guaranteed failure aborts before publishing (no broken listing).
3. **Desktop bounded retry** — `spawn_file_meta_reencrypt` (Rust) now retries transient failures (5 attempts, exp backoff + jitter, lock released across sleep), with the same dest-key idempotency check; decrypt-under-neither-key is terminal. In-memory per the todo's scope call (not a new `JournalOp`).
4. **Idempotent-by-id restore add** *(adversarial-review catch)* — my reorder opened a new post-publish failure window where a retry would double-list the file (same id, renamed). Fixed by dropping any prior copy of the child id before the add, so a retry replaces rather than duplicates.

  "content": "## Recovery hardening for move/restore re-encryption (`f6c720f48`)\n\nCompleted the partial-failure-recovery follow-up flagged by the CodeRabbit review of this PR — three changes, plus one fix surfaced by an adversarial self-review of the diff:\n\n1. **Shared idempotent re-key helper** (`packages/sdk/src/reencrypt.ts`) used by both `moveItem` and `restoreFromBin`. If the source-key resolve fails to decrypt, it confirms the record under the **destination** key and treats the re-key as already complete — so a retry after a partial failure completes instead of throwing. Non-decrypt errors (e.g. missing record) still propagate.\n\n2. **`restoreFromBin` reorder** — publish target → re-key → remove from bin (mirrors `moveItem`), with preconditions validated up front so a guaranteed failure aborts *before* publishing. At every intermediate failure the file stays readable from somewhere that lists it under the matching key (the bin, by the source key, before the re-key; the target, by the target key, after) — never readable from neither.\n\n3. **Desktop bounded retry** (`spawn_file_meta_reencrypt`, Rust FUSE/WinFsp) — transient resolve/fetch/publish errors retry with exponential backoff (5 attempts), the coordinator lock released across the backoff sleep; a record undecryptable under *both* keys is terminal (not retried). In-memory retry, not a durable journal entry (intentional scope — see the completed todo).\n\n4. **Idempotent-by-id restore add** — the reorder opened a post-publish window where a retry of a partially-applied restore would double-list the file (same id, renamed by the collision handler) since the no-conflict publish path doesn't dedup by id. Fixed by dropping any prior copy of the child id before the add, so a retry **replaces** rather than duplicates. (`moveItem` was checked and does not have this issue — it commits dest state after the re-key, so a retry reconciles via the CAS merge.)\n\nVerified: `tsc` + `eslint` clean; SDK unit tests pass (added idempotent-retry / reorder / no-duplicate-on-retry tests for both move and restore); `cargo check` + crate tests under the `fuse` feature pass. CI E2E dispatched against this branch.\n"
}
